what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the person's posts in tools/social-posts, read from their own post records through the run's records door.

payload.label: Posting calendar
payload.job: Show what this person is posting between two times, and which drafts have no time yet, so a post can be given a time or moved to another
payload.description: Give from and to (dates and times with their zone) and records (the person's post records). Returns posts: each post whose scheduled time falls in between (or, sent without a time, when it was sent), earliest first, with at, status, words and can_move; and unscheduled: the drafts and approved posts with no time yet. A post gets a new time through draft_post with post_id and scheduled_for, which makes an approved or scheduled post a draft again to approve. Its screen is the month and hour calendar, where a post is dragged to its time.

from.description: The start of the span, like 2026-10-01T00:00:00-04:00

to.description: The end of the span, after from

records.description: The person's post records, as the caller read them from a store ({ id, type: 'post', value }). The run keeps nothing.

provenance.source: trillion media-workspace scheduled-calendar.mjs and calendar-placement.mjs (the Mac's Schedule month, week and day views), rebuilt on src/social-posts.mjs calendar, the same read list_post_calendar makes (a2fdfe6), ported to the records door

screen.label: Posting calendar
screen.about: When each of your posts goes out.

payload.label: How each post did
payload.job: Show how each of this person's published posts did in each place it went: that place's own counts, the visitors its link brought and what they bought
payload.description: Give observations (each place's own counts for a post, read with that place's tools: { post_id, account_id, metrics: { name: number }, observed_at } or { platform_post_id, account_id?, metrics }), visits and conversions (as tool:break-down-visits-and-sales takes them: { visitor, project?, signals: { utm_content, ... } } and { visitor, project?, value? }) and optionally post_ids. Reads the person's post records handed in as `records` and returns posts: one row per place a post was published to that has a count, a visit or a conversion, with post_id, account_id, title, platform_post_id, url, metrics, observed_at, brought ({ visits, conversions, value }, only what was counted) and evidence. A visit counts for a place only when its utm_content is exactly that post's post_id (the post went to one place), the place's own post id, or post_id::account_id; a token that could name several places counts for none. Nothing missing is shown as zero.

post_ids.description: Only these posts (post_id values from tool:read-post-calendar)

observations.description: Each place's own counts for a post

visits.description: First-touch visits with their link signals

conversions.description: Sign-ups or sales by visitor, with value

records.description: The person's post records, as the caller read them from a store ({ id, type: 'post', value }). The run keeps nothing.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/content-analytics read-data/post-performance-attribution.ts (the join, unchanged but for its local types), read over the person's post records through the records door

payload.label: Where a post can go
payload.job: List the accounts this person can post to, each ready or not and why, and each place they have no account for yet
payload.description: Reads the person's connection records handed in as `records`. Returns destinations: each account_id (the connection id), platform, label, name and ready, with said when it is not ready (a field the place needs that the connection lacks); not_connected: each place with no account yet; and said. Use the account_id values as tool:draft-a-post destinations. It changes nothing.

records.description: The person's connection records, as the caller read them from a store ({ id, type: 'connection', value }). The run keeps nothing.

payload.label: Draft a post
payload.job: Work out a post as a draft for the person to look at (its words, its video or picture, where it goes and when) and answer the post row to keep
payload.description: Give caption (the words), media (the file as the person's files list it: { identity, name?, media_type?, byte_length? }) with media_facts ({ duration_seconds, width, height } the file does not say), destinations (account_id values from tool:list-post-destinations), caption_by_platform ({ platform: words }), settings_by_platform ({ platform: { ... } }, like a video title), link (an https page; it is added after the words, tagged with the post and the place), scheduled_for (a date and time with its zone), time_zone, source ({ kind, id } of the record it came from, kept as given), format_id, reaches (the people it contacts first, each with where they were found) and drafted_by (the AI writing it). Give post_id to change a draft; changing an approved post, or a scheduled one nothing was sent for, makes it a draft again. Returns post, ready (as tool:check-a-post gives it), said, and the post row to store under `keep`. Give records: the person's connection records, and the post when post_id changes one. Nothing is posted or stored here.

post_id.description: A post_id from tool:draft-a-post or tool:read-post-calendar

payload.label: Approve a post
payload.job: Check a drafted post is approved exactly as it was reviewed and answer the approved post row to keep
payload.description: Give post_id and expected_values (the complete approval_values of the post as it was reviewed); expected_values is required, and approval is refused when its words, file, destinations or time changed since. A post going nowhere yet is refused. approved_by names who approved it. Returns post, said and the approved post row to store under `keep`. Give records: the post. Give database to approve in that pursuit database: the post and the person's approval setting are read there and the answer is kept there, so no caller can carry an auto setting in.

The computer opens it with the login its vault holds as that name and -connection. The post's new state and one approval-decision row are kept in it. Without it the ask answers from the records given, as before.

payload.label: Publish a post now
payload.job: Work out queuing an approved post for immediate sending through each destination's existing send row and answer the post row to keep
payload.description: Give post_id and expected_values (the complete approval_values snapshot reviewed for this action). It is refused if the post changed, is not approved, or is not ready for every destination. When ready, it sets the post's time to now and queues the existing at-its-time wake; this action itself sends nothing and does not say the post was published. The queued post row comes back under `keep` for the caller to store, and each destination's send row answers its own outcome. Repeating the same request while it is queued returns the existing state without arming another send. A destination whose outcome is not known is never sent again automatically. Give records: the post and the person's connection records. Returns post_id, status, post, ready, said and keep.

expected_values.description: The complete approval_values from the post as reviewed

payload.description: Give post_id of an approved post whose scheduled_for is still ahead. payload.label: Use a snippet
payload.job: Fill in one of my snippets with this time's names and give me its words to put in what I am writing
payload.description: Give snippet_id (the snippet's id as the store keeps it) and values: { name: words } for each {name} blank. Returns snippet_id, title, text (the words with every given blank filled wherever it appears), left_blank (the blanks given no value, left exactly as written) and said naming them, so nothing is sent with a hole unseen. It counts and stores nothing and never changes the snippet's words. It sends nothing. Give records: the snippet's record. Refuses an unknown snippet_id.

payload.label: Read a conversation summary
payload.job: Read the summary kept of this conversation and whether newer messages have come since it was written
payload.description: Give conversation_id (and app) and message_times: the times of the conversation's newest messages as the messages owner shows them (its newest page, like the last 100, is enough). Returns summary (null when none is kept yet), newer_messages (how many of message_times come after the message the summary covers through), stale (newer_messages above 0) and said, so a stale summary is never taken for the conversation's present. Give records: the summary's record. Changes nothing.

payload.label: List my YouTube videos
payload.job: List the videos of the person's own YouTube channel, public, unlisted and private as the connection allows, with each video's title and privacy status
payload.description: Lists the videos of the channel the person's youtube connection signs in as, from the channel's uploads playlist (give the playlist_id that tool:check-a-connection returns for place youtube), page by page. Each video comes back with its id, title, privacy status (public, unlisted or private) and publish time; unlisted and private videos come back when the sign-in has read access to the channel, and a refusal means it does not. It posts nothing and changes nothing.

account_id.description: One of the person's accounts of this kind, service_connection:youtube or service_connection:youtube:<account>

playlist_id.description: The channel's uploads playlist id, from tool:check-a-connection (place youtube)

page_token.description: The nextPageToken the list before gave, for the next page

payload.label: Read the comments on a YouTube video
payload.job: Read the top-level comment threads of one YouTube video, with each comment's text, like count, publish time and the commenter's channel id
payload.description: Reads the top-level comment threads of one video (give its video_id), newest first, 100 to a page; give the nextPageToken the page before returned as page_token for the next page, until none comes back. Each thread carries the comment's text, like count, publish time, reply count and the commenter's channel id; YouTube is asked to leave out the commenter's display name and picture. A video with comments turned off comes back as a refusal from YouTube. To read many videos, run it once per video id: YouTube's comment threads are asked for one video at a time. It posts, rates and moderates nothing and changes nothing.

account_id.description: One of the person's accounts of this kind, service_connection:youtube or service_connection:youtube:<account>

video_id.description: The id of the video whose comments to read

page_token.description: The nextPageToken the page before gave, for the next page

payload.label: Send a post
payload.job: Send one of the person's approved posts to one of their accounts at a place once its time has come, and answer where it went as the post to keep
payload.description: Give post_id (an approved or scheduled post whose time has come), place (the slug of one of the places in read-data/post-places.json, as tool:list-post-destinations names them) and account_id (one of the post's destinations: a connection of that place's kind, service_connection:<vendor> or service_connection:<vendor>:<account>). The engine hands this run only that account's held values, chosen by place; they reach only that place's hosts, as each request leaves. A destination the post carries as not known is never sent again by itself: give resend: true only after looking at the place. This run reads the post and the connection from the rows it is given as `stored` and stores nothing: the post as it ends (each destination's outcome) comes back under `keep`, and the place gets an idempotency key made from the post, the account and the attempt. A destination that already has the post is not sent it again. A post with a file needs media_url, an address the caller made of that file where the person keeps it (a share such as a signed link, valid until the place has fetched it): the place is handed that address, or the bytes streamed from it, never a copy kept here; with no address, nothing is sent. Returns post_id, status, post (with each destination's status, url and error in plain words), said and keep. This posts publicly on the person's account: run it only with the person's yes for this post.

post_id.description: A post_id from tool:draft-a-post or tool:read-post-calendar

place.description: The place to send to: the slug of a row of read-data/post-places.json (its id without post-place:). It must be the place account_id's connection belongs to

resend.description: Send again to a destination whose outcome is not known, after looking on the place

armed_at.description: Given by the timed run of workflow:send-each-post-at-its-time when it runs this at the post's time: the armed_at the post was set with. Nothing is sent once the post no longer carries it

records.description: The person's rows this run reads, read by the caller from where the person keeps them (the engine keeps none): each { id, type, value } of a post (type post) and of the destination's connection (type connection), as the caller read them. What is not given is not there.

media_url.description: For a post with a file: an https address of that file made where the person keeps it (a share such as a signed link, which ranges), valid until the place has fetched it

keep.description: The rows to store, each { id, type, value } with the whole row as value; absent when nothing changed

payload.label: Check a connection
payload.job: Check that the person's connection to a place still reaches its account, before a post is set to go there or a read is made
payload.description: Asks the place which account the person's connection signs in as: give place (the slug of a place in read-data/post-places.json that declares a check) and account_id (one of the person's accounts of that place's kind, from tool:list-post-destinations). It asks with the value the person's vault holds for it, placed only as the request leaves, never shown. Returns what the place answers (the account's id and name or username; for YouTube also the channel's uploads playlist id). A refusal (an expired, revoked or under-scoped sign-in) means the person connects that place again. It posts nothing and changes nothing.

place.description: The place to ask: the slug of a row of read-data/post-places.json that has a check

account_id.description: One of the person's accounts of that place's kind, service_connection:<vendor> or service_connection:<vendor>:<account>, from tool:list-post-destinations

Returns posts: each with post_id, status, scheduled_for and caption. Reads only what it is given; changes nothing.
